# Terminal (`apps/one-terminal`) — agent context

The Terminal is a tiling window manager: one OS window hosting a transparent **chrome
webview** (React, lowest z-order) plus N **panel webviews** (each an isolated widget URL)
layered on top. Architecture overview: [README.md](../../apps/one-terminal/README.md). Rust side:
[src-tauri/AGENTS.md](../../apps/one-terminal/src-tauri/AGENTS.md). Rules: [docs/conventions/react.md](../../docs/conventions/react.md).

## Ground rules

- **Rust owns layout state.** The React app never mutates the layout locally — it calls a
  Tauri command, Rust mutates the `LayoutNode` tree, and emits `wm:layout` /
  `wm:host-layout`, which the chrome re-renders from. Don't add optimistic local copies.
- **One bundle, several webviews.** `index.html` serves both the chrome and the overlay
  webview (gated on `location.hash === "#overlay"` in `main.tsx`); `popout.html` /
  `popout.tsx` serves popped-out widget windows. Per-webview bootstrap must check which
  one it is running in.
- **Cross-webview state goes through Tauri events**, e.g. theme changes
  (`THEME_CHANGED_EVENT`). Guard against echo loops: only emit on direct user input.
- Widget-facing UI (headers, tab menus) must work in both the Terminal and popout entries —
  register extensions from `src/registerWidgetExtensions.ts`, which both entries import.

## Layout

```
src/App.tsx, main.tsx      chrome + overlay entry
src/popout.tsx             popout window entry (PopoutApp)
src/components/            layers (TabStripLayer, SplitterHandleLayer, DropZoneLayer, …), dialogs, menus
src/commands/              command registry, keybindings, keyboard/global-shortcut listeners
src/hooks/                 useLayout, useHostLayout, useDashboards, useAppDirectory, …
src/lib/                   non-React helpers (desktop agents, widget registry, config)
src/theme/                 theme store
src-tauri/                 Rust window manager
```

## Widget UI extension points

Two static registries in `src/components/` let developers customise per-app UI without touching the shell layout.

### Custom widget headers — `panelHeaders.tsx`

Controls what renders in the panel header bar (the draggable title bar above the webview content area) **and** inside each tab label. Add an entry keyed by FDC3 `appId`:

```tsx
// panelHeaders.tsx
const REGISTRY: Record<string, PanelHeaderContent> = {
  "my-app-id": ({ title }) => (
    <>
      <span className="wm-panel-header__badge">BADGE</span>
      <span className="wm-panel-header__title">{title}</span>
    </>
  ),
};
```

`PanelHeaderContent = (props: { appId: string; title: string }) => ReactNode`

The shell (`PanelHeaderLayer`) always provides the drag region and close button; the registered component renders only the content area inside them.

### Custom tab context-menu items — `contextMenuItems.ts`

Adds extra buttons to the right-click menu on a tab, rendered after the built-in Rename / Zoom / Channel / Keep running groups and before Pop out / Dock back. The same menu (`WidgetMenuItems.tsx`) is shown in a popped-out widget's window, so register items in a feature file imported from `src/registerWidgetExtensions.ts` — it is loaded by both the Terminal entry (`main.tsx`) and the popout entry (`popout.tsx`). Use `"*"` to target all apps:

```ts
// a feature file imported from src/registerWidgetExtensions.ts
import { registerCtxMenuItems } from "./components/contextMenuItems";
import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";

registerCtxMenuItems("my-app-id", [
  {
    label: "Reload",
    onClick: ({ label }, dismiss) => {
      // a command you add yourself — not built in
      invoke("wm_reload_panel", { label }).catch(console.error);
      dismiss();
    },
  },
  {
    label: "Force close",
    danger: true,
    onClick: ({ label }, dismiss) => {
      invoke("close_tab", { label }).catch(console.error);
      dismiss();
    },
  },
]);
```

`CtxMenuContext` fields available in `onClick`:

| Field         | Type                  | Description                                  |
| ------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `appId`       | `string`              | FDC3 App Directory identifier                |
| `label`       | `string`              | Webview label — stable ID for Tauri commands |
| `title`       | `string`              | App-provided title                           |
| `displayName` | `string \| undefined` | User-set override; `undefined` = no override |
| `stackPath`   | `number[]`            | Path to the containing Stack node            |
| `nTabs`       | `number`              | Number of tabs in the stack                  |
| `floating`    | `boolean`             | Widget is popped out (`stackPath` is `[]`)   |
| `group`       | `string \| undefined` | Glue group id of a glued popout; else unset  |

**Epic 08 note:** this registry will be superseded by `window.OT.plugins.get("contextMenu")` once the dynamic plugin system lands. Static entries will continue to work unchanged.

## Tests

```sh
npm run test:terminal                              # vitest run (jsdom, Tauri IPC mocked)
npm -w @one-terminal/one-terminal run test:watch
```

Tests live next to the code (`src/**/<name>.test.ts(x)`); setup in `src/test/`. Patterns:
[docs/conventions/react.md](../../docs/conventions/react.md#tests).

## Ships to scaffolded workspaces

This whole app is extracted into the scaffolder's `shared` overlay. Changes here drift the
templates — see [packages/create-one-terminal/AGENTS.md](../../packages/create-one-terminal/AGENTS.md).
